info.title: Kivly Public API
info.description:
Kivly Public API: location-scoped integration access to customers, loyalty, catalog, promotions, orders, invoice lifecycle, multichannel campaigns, automatic notifications, gift cards, surveys, branches, reservations, waitlists, contact lists, cost control, expenses, suppliers, ingredients, recipes, dishes, inventory, production, product receipts, reconciliation, analytics and webhooks.

Start with POST /api/v1/auth/token using location credentials from the normal panel and then GET /api/v1/integration/context. The token is data.token, has token_type Bearer and expires in 3600 seconds. Keep credentials on your server; never expose them in a browser, mobile app or documentation explorer. Tokens do not grant panel, GraphQL or platform administration access. Named API keys created in Dashboard have resource-family read/write permissions, expiry and revocation. Legacy location credentials retain access to the published operations. All keys share the location rate limits.

Default integration budgets: 120 requests/minute and 5000 requests/hour per location, shared across tokens and servers. Token issuance: 20 requests/minute per source IP. Webhook tests: 5/minute per location. Limits can be configured by the operator; integration/context returns effective budgets. HTTP 429 includes Retry-After in seconds. Honor it with bounded backoff and jitter. Redis unavailability returns 503 for integrations. Additional edge/network limits may apply.

Endpoints under /public/ and the explicitly anonymous reward/event endpoints retain their separate storefront contract; a Public API token, when supplied, still enforces its location boundary. This is a versioned code contract: deploy the matching backend before publishing new operations.

post.description: Authenticates an integration with client credentials and returns an access token. Use the location's client_id and client_secret from the Kivly panel, not OAuth credentials issued by Shopify, MCP or another provider. Send JSON from your backend. No grant_type, IP registration or separate integration activation is required by this endpoint. The account and location must be active. Read data.token and send it as Authorization: Bearer <token>. Tokens expire after 3600 seconds; request a new token with the same credentials. There is no refresh token. Rotating either credential revokes existing Public API tokens. Credentials from the normal panel use production; staging credentials require separate provisioning. A 403 with generic Access denied may come from an upstream access rule: report UTC time, path and X-Request-ID/CF-Ray to Kivly support without sending the secret.

A legacy service fallback also tries personal_id if the initial lookup found no customer. Returns loyalty, promotions and user directly, with no data envelope. loyalty.balance is a monetary equivalent in minor units; points and visits are raw loyalty units. For POINT/MONEY the response includes points; for VISIT it includes visits. A missing customer, and some internal lookup failures, return HTTP 200 with zero balance, empty promotions and null user details. Do not treat that fallback as a successful customer match. The legacy MemberId/DisplayText/Rewards response can also occur for a missing location or an unexpected route error. Check the response shape before offering rewards. This is a read operation: it does not register a customer or redeem a reward. Integrators authenticate with a location-scoped Public API Bearer token.

post.description:
Submit a sale for loyalty processing. Send at least one item: omitted, null or empty items are rejected by the business validator even though the input model permits them. customer.id and customer.name are required input fields. Resolve the registered customer first: customer.id must be the Kivly ID returned by the customer lookup; an external ID belongs in customer.external_id (or external_customer_id). Matching tries external ID, then phone, then Kivly customer ID. Email alone is not used to match the invoice's customer. This endpoint does not register an unknown customer. Monetary totals (total, subtotal, discount) and item prices are integer minor units (1250 = EUR 12.50). Use a stable, unique code for each sale. Existing codes are detected on sequential retries, but this route does not provide a general exactly-once transaction guarantee. Do not retry ambiguous timeouts or send the same sale concurrently without reconciling its result. The operation processes loyalty before responding; a 200 business response can still have success=false. Accepted responses include points_earned and available_balance in the business's raw loyalty units (points, money minor units or visits). An already processed sale returns duplicate=true and points_earned=0. Rewards are handled before the duplicate transaction check, so duplicate detection does not guarantee that replaying promotions is side-effect free. total.tax is an integer VAT percentage, not a monetary amount. This is a loyalty sale operation, not fiscal invoice issuance.

post.description:
Import an immediate pickup/delivery order from your server using orders:write.

The business comes from the token. Supply its branch, menu and Kivly product IDs.
Prices and totals are gross integer cents declared by your channel; Kivly validates
arithmetic and resolves taxes and kitchen routing from its own configuration.
PAID_EXTERNALLY records payment collected outside Kivly; this endpoint never charges
a card. Unpaid orders enter the POS for collection. The menu's acceptance mode applies.
The order source is api; metadata.integration_channel identifies your website.
Reuse channel + external_id and the same body after a timeout (200 replay); a changed
body returns 409. A 503 can mean the order is saved but POS synchronization is pending:
retry the identical request. No provider dispatch, scheduled orders or table orders here.
Existing GET /orders/{order_id}, PATCH /orders/{order_id}/status and order.* webhooks
provide follow-up. A 201 confirms server/POS persistence, not physical printing.

InvoiceAuditEntry.description:
Una línea del historial. Se añade, nunca se toca.

Existe porque el `updated_at` de un documento contesta «cuándo» y ninguna de
las preguntas que de verdad se hacen en una revisión: quién la emitió, quién
la anuló y por qué, cuántas veces se intentó remitir.

InvoiceCancellation.title: InvoiceCancellation
InvoiceCancellation.description:
Anulación de una factura emitida.

Se guarda dentro de la factura y no la sustituye: la anulada tiene que seguir
apareciendo en cualquier listado de auditoría, con su número, marcada como
anulada. Un `delete` aquí sería un hueco en la serie que nadie sabría

InvoiceCompany.description:
Datos de la empresa emisora (o del negocio).

`address` es el **domicilio fiscal** de la sociedad, el que se da de alta en
el onboarding fiscal. `establishment_address` es dónde ocurrió la venta —la
dirección de la sucursal—, y sólo se guarda cuando no coincide con el
domicilio: una factura que repite dos veces la misma dirección con dos
etiquetas distintas confunde más que informa.

InvoiceCustomerCompany.title: InvoiceCustomerCompany
InvoiceCustomerCompany.description:
Datos del cliente (empresa o particular).

`postal_code` va aparte de `address` porque hay administraciones que lo piden
separado: TicketBAI tiene `CodigoPostal` y `Direccion` como dos elementos, y
en Gipuzkoa y Araba una factura con destinatario identificado y **sin
dirección se rechaza**. Es opcional para no invalidar las facturas ya
emitidas; cuando falta se intenta leer de `address`, y si no se puede leer con
seguridad se pide, en vez de adivinarlo: un código postal inventado viaja a
la hacienda foral igual que uno correcto.

InvoiceKind.description:
Qué clase de documento es, en términos de Kivly.

No se confunde con `InvoiceType` de la factura canónica: aquél es lo que el
adaptador necesita para construir su XML, y colapsa la sustitución dentro de
`FULL` porque lo que la distingue viaja en `references`. Aquí hace falta
separarlas porque **la interfaz ofrece acciones distintas** según cuál sea, y
porque una factura de sustitución tiene que poder encontrarse como tal en una
auditoría sin releer sus referencias.

IssueFullReplacementInput.title: IssueFullReplacementInput
IssueFullReplacementInput.description:
«El cliente pide factura» sobre un ticket ya emitido.

No modifica el ticket: crea una factura completa nueva, con su serie, su
número y su fecha de expedición, que **sustituye** a la simplificada. Las dos
quedan guardadas y enlazadas.

El ticket se identifica de una de dos formas, y hacen falta las dos porque en
Kivly una simplificada puede vivir en dos sitios distintos:

- `order_id` — el caso normal. La simplificada de una venta del TPV se
  declara al cerrar el pedido y su registro fiscal se guarda **en el propio
  pedido**: no hay documento en `invoices` hasta que alguien pide factura.
- `invoice_id` — cuando la simplificada sí es un documento, como en las
  facturas de enlace de pago.

LifecycleStatus.title: LifecycleStatus
LifecycleStatus.description:
¿Existe como documento fiscal? Lo decide Kivly.

Sólo hay dos valores y el paso entre ellos es de ida: al emitir se consume un
número de la serie y se encadena un registro, y eso no se deshace. Un tercer
valor tipo `CANCELLED` aquí sería el error clásico —una factura anulada
**sigue emitida**, y su número sigue consumido—; eso vive en el efecto fiscal.

  propio `last_reservation_buffer_min`).
- HOURS: se usan los `hours_overrides` de la zona y el buffer propio
  de ZoneSettings.

schedule_mode.description: Origen del horario de la zona: 'shifts' usa los ServiceShift del local; 'hours' usa `hours_overrides` propios de la zona.

last_reservation_buffer_min.title: Last Reservation Buffer Min
last_reservation_buffer_min.description: Minutos antes del cierre en los que ya no se admiten reservas nuevas cuando schedule_mode='hours' (semántica 'last admission'). La última reserva aceptada empieza en close − buffer; la duración (turn_time) puede extenderse más allá del cierre oficial. Si el valor es 0, se aplica el comportamiento legacy: la última reserva termina justo al cierre (start = close − turn_time). Con schedule_mode='shifts' prevalece el buffer del propio turno.

post.description: Kivly sends this request to the webhook URL configured for a location when a subscribed event occurs. Delivery uses a 30 second timeout, up to 3 retries, and a minimum 60 second retry delay (queue scheduling can add latency). Deliveries are persisted before sending; the event id and body remain stable on retries. Duplicates and out-of-order deliveries are possible. Deduplicate by payload.id after durable receipt and return any 2xx. Use HTTPS on port 443; redirects and private IPs are rejected. Verify X-Kivly-Signature-V2 as hex HMAC-SHA256 of timestamp + '.' + raw UTF-8 request body with webhook_token. Compare in constant time and reject timestamps more than 300 seconds from your clock. The legacy X-Kivly-Signature signs only the raw body and remains available for existing receivers.
